name: Open Graph Checker
title: Open Graph Checker: Validate Every og: Tag
description: Free Open Graph checker: validate og:title, og:description, og:image, og:url and og:type on any URL, catch broken tags and see the fix for each.
answer: An Open Graph checker reads a page's og: tags — the ones Facebook, LinkedIn, Slack and others use to build link previews — and flags missing, duplicate or broken values. Enter a URL to validate og:title, og:type, og:image and og:url, compare og:url with your canonical and see the preview.
trust: We fetch the page live, read every og: tag in the raw HTML and request the image it points to.
body:
## Open Graph Check: The 4 Tags Every Page Needs

The [Open Graph protocol](https://ogp.me/) defines four required properties for every page:

| Tag | What it is |
|---|---|
| og:title | The title as it should appear in the preview |
| og:type | The kind of object, usually website or article |
| og:image | The preview image URL |
| og:url | The canonical URL of the page |

og:description and og:site_name are optional but make a better card. Without the required tags, platforms guess — often picking the wrong image or a menu label as the title.

## Open Graph Debugger: Why the Wrong Image Shows Up

Four causes cover most cases:

1. **Duplicate tags** — a theme and an SEO plugin both output og:image, and platforms take the first.
2. **Wrong attribute** — the protocol uses `property="og:…"`; some platforms ignore `name=`.
3. **og:url disagrees with your canonical** — shares and previews split across two URLs.
4. **Cached old version** — platforms cache previews; Meta's [Sharing Debugger](https://developers.facebook.com/tools/debug/) and LinkedIn's [Post Inspector](https://www.linkedin.com/post-inspector/) can refresh theirs.

## How common are Open Graph tags?

Close to universal on big sites. In our October 2026 analysis of 315 big-brand homepages ([dataset](/resources/technical-seo-baseline-2026-10.json)), 90.8% set og:title, 90.5% og:description and 86.7% og:image.

The gaps are in the details: only 34.6% declared the image's width and height, which Meta uses to render the image on the first share.

## How do I read the result?

Fails are missing required tags or broken images; warnings are duplicates, `name=` attributes, long descriptions and og:url mismatches. The table lists every og: tag exactly as found, so you can spot the plugin that added a duplicate.

Fix the tags in your page head, then check the image itself with the [OG image checker](/tools/og-image-checker) and see the result on six platforms with the [link preview tool](/tools/link-preview).

faqs.a: Meta tags in a page's head, defined by the Open Graph protocol, that tell social platforms and messaging apps which title, description and image to show when the page is shared.

faqs.q: Do Open Graph tags help SEO?
faqs.a: Not as a Google ranking factor. They control how your links look when shared, which affects clicks from social and chat, and they give AI tools a clean summary of the page.

faqs.q: Why does Facebook show an old title after I changed my tags?
faqs.a: Facebook caches previews per URL. Run the URL through Meta's Sharing Debugger and choose "Scrape Again" to refresh the cached title, description and image.
